items.prompt: What do medicines do?

options.why: Medicines are for treating illness.

options.text: They can help treat some illnesses.
They give a person energy like food.
options.why: Food gives energy.

hints: Medicine is used when someone is ill.
It helps them get better.
It is not food.
items.explanation: Medicines can treat some illnesses when they are used correctly.

items.prompt: Why should you read the label on a medicine with an adult?

options.text: to see what colour it is
options.why: The colour is not the reason.

options.text: to use the right amount safely
to find out how it tastes
options.why: The taste is not the reason.

hints: Too much medicine can harm you.
The label says how much to take.
It keeps you safe.
items.explanation: The label tells you how much to take and when, so you can use the medicine safely.

items.prompt: Which of these helps keep you healthy?

options.why: Not moving is bad for health.
Fresh air and exercise help health.

hints: Think about what makes your heart strong.
Running and playing help.
Doing nothing does not.
items.explanation: Exercise keeps muscles, bones and the heart healthy.

items.prompt: Plants get their energy from the ___.
hints: Plants need light.
It shines in the day.
It is a star.
items.explanation: Plants get energy from sunlight.

items.prompt: What are germs?

options.text: dirt you can see on your hands
options.why: Germs are too small to see.

options.text: tiny living things that can cause disease

options.why: Germs are not medicines.

hints: They are too small to see.
Some of them make us ill.
They spread from one person to another.
items.explanation: Germs are tiny living things. Some of them cause infectious diseases.

items.prompt: Which can catch an infectious disease?

options.why: Plants and animals can catch diseases too.
People and plants can too.

hints: Think about plants that get spots on their leaves.
Animals can get ill too.
The answer includes all of them.
items.explanation: Plants, animals and people can all have infectious diseases.

items.prompt: Animals get the energy they need from...

options.why: Animals cannot use sunlight to make food.
Air does not give animals energy.

hints: Animals cannot make their own food.
They eat plants or other animals.
Think about what you eat.
items.explanation: Animals get energy from the food they eat.

items.prompt: Why is moving around good for your health?

options.why: Exercise does not mean sleeping less.

options.text: It keeps your muscles, bones and heart strong.
It makes your skin change colour.
options.why: This is not a health benefit.

hints: Think about what moves when you run.
Your heart works harder when you exercise.
Strong muscles help you move well.
items.explanation: Movement keeps the body strong, including the heart, muscles and bones.

items.prompt: What does a vaccine do?

options.text: It cures every illness at once.
options.why: A vaccine prevents some diseases. It does not cure all illness.

options.text: It helps the body get ready to fight a germ.
It kills all the good bacteria.
options.why: Vaccines do not do that.

hints: Vaccines are given before you catch a disease.
They help your body learn to fight.
They prevent some illnesses.
items.explanation: A vaccine prepares the body to fight a germ, so it can prevent some diseases.

items.prompt: Which of these can help stop the spread of infectious diseases?

options.why: This spreads germs.

options.text: sharing cups with someone who is ill
options.why: Sharing cups can spread germs.

hints: Think about stopping germs from moving.
Vaccines prepare the body.
Clean hands carry fewer germs.
items.explanation: Vaccines and washing hands both help stop germs spreading.

items.prompt: A farmer finds a disease spreading among his chickens. What is the best name for this kind of disease?

options.why: There is no such thing.
A medicine treats a disease.

hints: It spreads from animal to animal.
It is caused by germs.
The word starts with i.
items.explanation: A disease caused by germs that can spread is infectious.

items.prompt: How do plants get the energy they need to grow?

options.why: Most plants do not eat.

options.text: They use sunlight to make their own food.
They get energy from the wind.
options.why: Wind does not give plants energy.

hints: Plants need light.
Plants are producers.
They make food in their leaves.
items.explanation: Plants use energy from sunlight to make their own food.

items.prompt: A ___ can help prevent some diseases by getting the body ready to fight germs.
hints: It is given by a doctor or nurse.
It is often an injection.
The word starts with v.
items.explanation: A vaccine prepares the body to fight a germ before you catch the disease.

items.prompt: Why do doctors often tell people to finish a full course of medicine?

options.why: Taste is not the reason.
The reason is health.

hints: Stopping early can leave germs behind.
The illness might come back.
The course is planned by the doctor.
items.explanation: A full course gives the best chance of treating the illness properly.

items.prompt: Sort each item by where the living thing gets its energy.
hints: Plants make their own food using light.
Animals eat other living things.
Think about which ones can eat.
items.explanation: Animals get energy from food. Plants get energy from sunlight.

items.prompt: Why is it important to move around every day?

options.text: It stops you from catching any disease.
options.why: Exercise helps health but does not stop all diseases.

options.text: Movement helps keep the heart, muscles and bones healthy.
It makes your body stop needing food.
options.why: Your body still needs food.

hints: Think about what exercise does.
The heart is a muscle.
Bones get stronger when used.
items.explanation: Regular movement keeps the body healthy and strong.

items.prompt: Which of these is a safe way to use medicine?

options.text: take extra to get better faster
options.why: More is not better and can be dangerous.

options.text: take only the amount on the label, given by an adult
share it with a friend who feels the same
options.why: Medicine is chosen for one person.

hints: More is not always better.
Medicine is chosen for one person.
The label gives the right amount.
items.explanation: Use medicine only as directed and only for the person it was given to.

items.prompt: A plant in a dark cupboard becomes weak. What is the best explanation?

options.why: Plants do not catch colds.

options.text: It cannot get the energy it needs from sunlight.
It needs more food from the soil.
options.why: The problem is lack of light.

hints: Think about where plants get energy.
Plants need light to make food.
The cupboard has none.
items.explanation: Without light, a plant cannot get the energy it needs, so it becomes weak.

items.prompt: A vaccine and a medicine are different. Which statement shows the difference?

options.text: A vaccine treats every illness and a medicine prevents it.
options.why: It is the other way round.

options.text: A vaccine helps prevent a disease, and a medicine helps treat an illness.
They are exactly the same thing.
options.why: They do different jobs.

hints: One is used before you are ill.
One is used when you are ill.
Vaccines get the body ready.
items.explanation: Vaccines prepare the body to prevent some diseases. Medicines help treat an illness that has started.

items.prompt: Why can a disease spread quickly in a crowded classroom?

options.text: People in a crowd make germs.
options.why: Germs are not made by crowds.

options.text: Germs can pass easily from one person to another.
Germs are heavy so they fall on everyone.
options.why: Germs are tiny and spread by touch, air and shared things.

hints: Think about how close people are.
Germs move by touch or in the air.
More people means more chances to pass them on.
items.explanation: In a crowded room germs have more chances to pass from person to person.

items.prompt: True or false: Germs are tiny living things that can make you ill.
hints: Can you see germs by eye?
They make us sick.
Germs cause illness.
items.explanation: Some bacteria and viruses cause disease. They are too small to see without a microscope.

items.prompt: True or false: Antibiotics can cure illnesses caused by viruses such as a cold.
hints: What do antibiotics kill?
A cold is not caused by bacteria.
They do not work on viruses.
items.explanation: Antibiotics only work against bacteria. A cold is caused by a virus, so they do not help.

items.prompt: True or false: A vaccine helps the body get ready to fight a disease.
hints: Is it before or after the illness?
It prepares the body.
It trains the defences.
items.explanation: It teaches the body's defences to recognise a germ, so if it arrives later the body can fight it quickly.

items.prompt: True or false: Sneezing without covering your mouth does not spread germs.
hints: What flies out when you sneeze?
Can germs be in droplets?
It spreads germs.
items.explanation: A sneeze sends droplets with germs into the air, and others can breathe them in. Cover with a tissue or your elbow.
